conflict_topics: Scheduling exclusive use of the small room
Need for a closed door / private uninterrupted space (prayer and confidential calls)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants provide concrete constraints and reasons (e.g., client calls, prayer needs, unpredictability of file access).
Multiple practical proposals were offered: time-shifting (1:15), notification/advance-fetch, and moving files out of the room.
Some repetition of the same constraint ('I can't predict', 'door has to stay closed') but not excessive.
Speakers stayed on-topic and consistently referenced prior turns (good turn-taking and grounding).
evaluation.final_reason: Participants explored time-shifting and a notification/advance-fetch scheme. A, C and D accepted notifying B before room use (Rounds 10–11: 'That would work for me.'), but B repeatedly refused advance notice because file needs are unpredictable ('I can't guess what I'll need' — Turn 33). C proposed moving files out (Turn 34) but B did not agree. No mutually accepted arrangement for closed-door private use versus B's unpredictable file access was reached.
position_change_notes: Agent D started by requesting fixed slots and then showed flexibility (accepted 1 p.m., offered 5 p.m., then 1:15) — moved from fixed demand to negotiated times (evidence: Turns 2, 4, 8).
Agent C accepted shifting to 1:15 (Turn 9) and later proposed the notification/advance-fetch compromise (Turn 30) and an alternative of moving files (Turn 34).
Agent A consistently raised confidentiality concerns about client calls and accepted the notification scheme (Turns 1, 26, 32); A did not reverse position.
Agent B consistently maintained that advance notice 'doesn't work' due to unpredictability and did not change that stance during the run (Turns 6, 14, 20, 29, 33).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A says 4:30 'could be a problem' and 1 p.m. 'should be fine' (Turn 1). Agent D accepts 1 p.m. and proposes 5 p.m. instead (Turn 2) — schedule incompatibility has appeared but is still negotiable.
Agent A: '5 p.m. could also be a problem' (Turn 3). Agent D suggests 4 p.m. (Turn 4). The afternoon slot remains contested and the incompatibility persists.

Agent A: 'That's when they start' about 4 p.m. (Turn 5). Agent B introduces a new constraint: 'I need to get to the files in that room all day. My work is in there.' (Turn 6). Multiple competing needs now create clearer disagreement.

Agent C states a daily need at 1 p.m. (Turn 7). Agent D offers flexibility: 'Could I use it at 1:15 then, after your call?' (Turn 8). D's flexibility softens the scheduling conflict but B's file access remains unresolved.

Agent C agrees to 1:15 (Turn 9). D asks B whether B would need to get in/out during that specific time (Turn 10). A partial agreement between C and D reduces conflict on the 1 p.m. block, though B's unpredictability is not yet addressed.

Agent B: 'I can't really say. I just go in to get files whenever I need them.' (Turn 14). Agent D proposes notifying B 'just before I go in' so B could take needed files (Turn 15) — an accommodation attempt, not yet accepted by B.

Agent D clarifies the need: prayer 'private, quiet space... door has to be closed. I can't be interrupted.' (Turn 18). Agent B: 'That doesn't really work. I don't know what I'll need ahead of time.' (Turn 20). This makes an explicit, strong incompatibility between closed-door privacy and B's unpredictable immediate access.

Agent D: 'Then I can't use the room. If the door might be opened at any time, it's not a private space.' (Turn 21). Agent C supports the need for an uninterrupted closed door for calls (Turn 24). The practical conflict hardens: private use vs. unpredictable shared access.
Agent A: 'My client calls are confidential. The door has to stay closed.' (Turn 26). Agent C asks B about frequency (Turn 28), but B's unpredictability remains the same; no settlement yet.

Agent B: 'It changes... I can't predict it.' (Turn 29). Agent C proposes notifying B ahead and taking files for 'say, half hour' so others get 10–15 minutes private (Turn 30) — a concrete compromise attempt that softens the impasse but awaits acceptance from B.

Agent D: 'Yes, that's what I suggested. That would work for me.' (Turn 31). Agent A: 'That works for me too.' (Turn 32). Several parties accept the notification approach, but Agent B has not accepted and previously rejected it.

Agent B repeats 'I already said that doesn't work for me. I can't guess what I'll need.' (Turn 33). Agent C proposes moving the files out so B can access them anytime (Turn 34) — a new practical solution, but there is no acceptance from B, so the core conflict remains unresolved.

substantive_insights: Core tension is between requirements for an uninterrupted, closed-door private space (for prayer and confidential calls) and a coworker’s legitimately unpredictable need to access files in that same private room.
Time-shifting and short notification windows can satisfy scheduled private calls but do not solve genuinely unpredictable instantaneous access needs.
Physical relocation of files is a viable technical fix if the file-owner consents; that change would remove the unpredictability but requires B's agreement and operational effort.
